note: Rules extracted from the two books; each rule with PDF pages. Conditions in 'when' are script filters (heuristic [inference] for n/p).

rules.situation: Goal = inference (understand which predictors matter, the sign and shape of the relationship)
rules.recommendation: Prefer restricted, interpretable models (linear regression, lasso); very flexible models (splines, boosting) make it harder to understand each predictor.

rules.situation: Goal = prediction only
rules.recommendation: The most flexible method does not always predict best: excess flexibility causes overfitting; compare by estimated test error.

rules.situation: Any problem
rules.recommendation: No method dominates on every dataset; decide by estimated test error (validation, CV), not by preference.

rules.situation: Quantitative response, n much larger than p, approximately linear relationship
rules.recommendation: Least squares has low bias and low variance; use the diagnostics of ch. 3 (residuals, leverage, VIF).

rules.situation: n is not much larger than p (n ≈ p)
rules.recommendation: The variance of least squares blows up and overfitting occurs: use ridge, lasso, subset/forward or dimension reduction.

rules.situation: p > n
rules.recommendation: Do not use least squares, the F statistic, Cp/AIC/BIC or adjusted R²; use forward stepwise, ridge, lasso or PCR (for classification, the ESL also offers diagonal LDA and nearest shrunken centroids); evaluate on an independent test set/CV; do not over-interpret the selected variables.

rules.situation: Many predictors, but only a few with a large effect
rules.recommendation: Tends to favor the lasso (zeroes out the irrelevant ones); confirm by CV because the number of relevant predictors is unknown.

rules.situation: Response depends on many predictors of similar size
rules.recommendation: Tends to favor ridge; confirm by CV.

rules.situation: Correlated predictors / collinearity
rules.recommendation: Diagnose with VIF (above 5 or 10 is problematic); drop or combine variables; ridge stabilizes the coefficients of correlated variables.

rules.situation: Need to select variables and keep interpretability
rules.recommendation: Lasso or subset selection; the lasso produces sparse models; forward selection works even with large p.

rules.situation: Many predictors (large p) and wanting best subset
rules.recommendation: Best subset is infeasible above ~40 predictors (2^p models); use stepwise or lasso.

rules.situation: Non-linear relationship in one predictor
rules.recommendation: Low-degree polynomial or splines (natural, knots at quantiles, number of knots/df by CV); splines tend to beat high-degree polynomials.

rules.situation: Several predictors, non-linearity, want to interpret each effect
rules.recommendation: GAM (additive); add interactions by hand (X_j·X_k) if needed; for general interactions, forest or boosting.

rules.situation: Suspected interaction (synergy) between predictors
rules.recommendation: Include an interaction term respecting the hierarchical principle (keep the main effects) or use trees/boosting.

rules.situation: Binary response, linear boundary, approximately normal predictors
rules.recommendation: LDA can improve on logistic regression when normality holds approximately.

rules.situation: Binary response, clearly non-Gaussian predictors
rules.recommendation: Logistic regression can outperform LDA; in the Student t scenario QDA deteriorates.

rules.situation: Well-separated classes
rules.recommendation: Logistic regression estimates become unstable (in the limit, infinite); LDA does not suffer from this problem. SVM tends to do well with well-separated classes; with overlapping classes logistic regression is often preferred.

rules.situation: Small n and approximately normal predictors within each class
rules.recommendation: LDA is more stable than logistic regression.

rules.situation: More than two classes
rules.recommendation: LDA is popular (multiclass logistic regression is little used); do not use linear regression on indicators with K ≥ 3 without checking for masking.

rules.situation: Moderately non-linear boundary
rules.recommendation: QDA: better if the training set is large or if the common Σ is clearly false; LDA is the better bet with few observations (QDA estimates K·p(p+1)/2 covariances).

rules.situation: Very non-linear boundary
rules.recommendation: KNN with K chosen by CV (K = 1 was the worst in scenario 6); other non-parametric methods (SVM with kernel, trees/boosting); KNN does not say which predictors matter.

rules.situation: Imbalanced classes or asymmetric error costs
rules.recommendation: Do not trust the overall error (the null classifier errs 3.33% on Default); examine the confusion matrix, sensitivity, specificity, ROC/AUC and adjust the threshold (0.5 → 0.2 reduced missed defaulters from 75.7% to 41.4%) according to the costs.

rules.situation: Need probabilities
rules.recommendation: Logistic regression and LDA estimate posteriors; the SVM hinge loss estimates the classifier, not probabilities; the share of bagging votes is not a calibrated probability.

rules.situation: Need interpretation and easy communication, non-linear relationship
rules.recommendation: A small tree (easy to explain and visualize), knowing that accuracy is usually lower and the tree is unstable.

rules.situation: Want the best accuracy from trees
rules.recommendation: Bagging, random forest or boosting; forests are simpler to tune and, in many problems, similar to boosting (which usually wins with tuning).

rules.situation: Random forest
rules.recommendation: m ≈ √p (classification) or p/3 (regression), minimum node size 1 (classification) or 5 (regression), but treat m as a tuning parameter; increase B until the OOB error stabilizes (there is no overfitting from B).

rules.situation: Boosting
rules.recommendation: Learn slowly: λ = 0.01 or 0.001 (ESL: ν < 0.1), B by CV/early stopping, small trees (d = 1 gives an additive model; ESL: 4 ≤ J ≤ 8), subsampling ≈ 0.5; boosting can overfit if B is large.

rules.situation: Noisy labels or outliers in the response
rules.recommendation: Avoid AdaBoost/exponential loss; prefer binomial deviance (classification) and absolute or Huber loss (regression).

rules.situation: Messy data: mixed types, missing values, outliers in the predictors, many irrelevant predictors, large N
rules.recommendation: Trees come closest to an off-the-shelf method (Table 10.1); neural networks and SVM do poorly on these characteristics.

rules.situation: Interpretation is not needed and predictive power is the focus
rules.recommendation: Neural networks, SVM and kNN/kernels have good predictive power (Table 10.1), but little interpretability and little robustness to irrelevant inputs.

rules.situation: Using an SVM
rules.recommendation: Choose C (and γ in the radial kernel) by CV: high γ improves the training fit and may worsen the test error; C is not an 'irrelevant' parameter.

rules.situation: SVM with many noise features
rules.recommendation: The SVM with a polynomial kernel is sensitive to the degree and to noise; adaptive methods (additive/MARS) degrade less in the ESL example.

rules.situation: Choose a model or hyperparameter
rules.recommendation: Cross-validation with k = 5 or 10 (good compromise between bias and variance); LOOCV has high variance.

rules.situation: Few observations (e.g., N = 50)
rules.recommendation: 5-fold CV trains on 40 observations and may overestimate the error if the learning curve is still steep.

rules.situation: There is variable selection, supervised filters or hyperparameter tuning
rules.recommendation: Repeat the whole sequence (selection included) inside each fold; only unsupervised filters can stay outside; keep an untouched test set for the final error.

rules.situation: Lots of data
rules.recommendation: Split into training, validation and test (typical split 50%/25%/25%); use the test set only at the end.

rules.situation: Compare linear models by information criterion
rules.recommendation: Cp/AIC and BIC (BIC penalizes more and chooses smaller models; BIC is consistent, AIC tends toward complex models); CV is more general because it needs neither counting df nor estimating σ².

rules.situation: CV error curve flat around the minimum
rules.recommendation: One-standard-error rule: choose the simplest model whose error is within one standard error of the minimum.

rules.situation: Need a standard error or CI for an estimator with no formula
rules.recommendation: Bootstrap (B samples with replacement of size n; SE = standard deviation of the estimates).

rules.situation: Testing thousands of variables individually (e.g., genes)
rules.recommendation: Control the FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg; permutation p-values) instead of Bonferroni, which is too conservative with large M; FDR is not type I error.

rules.situation: Correlated errors (time series)
rules.recommendation: Standard errors, CIs and p-values become optimistic; plot residuals against time.

rules.situation: Non-constant error variance (funnel in the residuals)
rules.recommendation: Transform Y (log or square root) or use weighted least squares.

rules.situation: Outliers or influential points
rules.recommendation: Studentized residuals with absolute value > 3 are suspect; mean leverage (p+1)/n; an outlier with high leverage is dangerous; remove only if it is a data collection error.

rules.situation: PCA for exploration or preprocessing
rules.recommendation: Center and, in general, standardize (sd = 1) before PCA; choosing the number of components by 'elbow' is subjective; in PCR, choose M by CV.

rules.situation: Clustering
rules.recommendation: K-means with several random initializations; for hierarchical clustering prefer average or complete linkage; test dissimilarities (Euclidean vs correlation), standardization and subsets; treat the clusters as a hypothesis and validate.

rules.situation: Choose the number of clusters K
rules.recommendation: CV does not work (W_K always decreases); look for an elbow in W_K or use the gap statistic; K may come from the problem (segmentation).

rules.situation: Only distances between objects (no coordinates)
rules.recommendation: K-medoids (or hierarchical) instead of K-means.

rules.situation: Many correlated variables and a response tied to the directions of largest variance
rules.recommendation: PCR (M components by CV, with standardization); PLS rarely beats ridge or PCR.

rules.situation: Any method with a tuning parameter (λ, M, K, C, depth)
rules.recommendation: Choose the parameter by cross-validation over a grid and refit the final model on all the data.

rules.situation: Doubt between logistic regression and LDA
rules.recommendation: Logistic regression makes fewer assumptions and is considered the safer, more robust bet; LDA gains efficiency if the Gaussian model holds, but is not robust to gross outliers.

rules.situation: You believe the relationship is (nearly) linear
rules.recommendation: If f is linear, linear regression is unbiased and hard to beat; KNN wins only with appreciable non-linearity.

rules.situation: Adaptive models (trees) and test error
rules.recommendation: AIC is impractical (df is hard); CV and bootstrap can underestimate the error by ~10% in these cases: only a separate test set is unbiased.
